query: For Q235 steel in its pre-exposure state, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain the onset or suppression of corrosion-related degradation in harsh environments at room and elevated temperatures? Specify a controlled study that would isolate the governing cause, predicted observations relative to the untreated reference, applicable boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification result.

generation.hypothesis: The adsorption of organic corrosion inhibitors, such as imidazole derivatives, onto the surface of Q235 steel can effectively suppress corrosion-related degradation in harsh environments at room and elevated temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: Q235 steel in its pre-exposure state
generation.intervention: Application of organic corrosion inhibitors, such as imidazole derivatives
generation.conditions: Harsh environments, including high temperatures and presence of corrosive substances
generation.structural_mediator: Adsorption of organic corrosion inhibitors onto the metal surface
generation.mechanism: Formation of a protective layer on the metal surface, preventing corrosion
generation.predicted_outcome: Reduced corrosion rate and improved corrosion resistance
generation.baseline: Untreated Q235 steel in harsh environments
generation.boundary: Temperature range: room temperature to elevated temperatures; presence of corrosive substances
generation.uncertainty: Effectiveness of organic corrosion inhibitors in extremely harsh environments, such as high-temperature and high-pressure conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled study with treated and untreated Q235 steel samples exposed to harsh environments
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated samples show no significant reduction in corrosion rate compared to the untreated samples, the hypothesis is falsified

Most organic inhibitors adsorb to metal substrates via either physical adsorption means (such as electrostatic interactions) or chemical adsorption (such as coordination bonds). The free lone pair of electrons of the inhibitor molecules are of vital importance to corrosion inhibition [].
Imidazole derivatives have emerged as promising corrosion inhibitors due to their high corrosion inhibition efficiency in an acidic corrosive medium and their non-toxic nature. Such organic compounds contain heteroatoms (N, O, S, and P), polar functional groups, or unsaturated bonds in their structures [,,,]. Therefore, they readily adhere to the metal surfaces with electrostatic attraction between the inhibitor and the metal (physisorption) or by transferring electrons and forming coordinate covalent bonds (chemisorption), leading to the formation of a protective layer on the metal surface that enhances the alloy’s corrosion resistance [,,,]. Nevertheless, the investigated corrosive medium is relatively mild with respect to the industrial pickling process of metals, and it is unknown whether N,S-CDs can still effectively inhibit the metal corrosion under more harsh environments.
Hence, in this study, N,S-CDs were prepared by a hydrothermal method with citric acid monohydrate (CA·H2O) and thiourea as precursors. The synthesized N,S-CDs were characterized using scanning probe microscopy (SPM), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) and ultraviolet-visible (UV-vis) spectroscopy. The corrosion behavior of Q235 carbon steel in 1 M HCl solution with different concentrations of N,S-CDs was evaluated by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), potentiodynamic polarization tests and weight loss measurement, exhibiting a high inhibition efficiency of 96.6%.
